body:
Triage: 摘 `finding`(卡已入决策箱,双态混编会顶乱两个读数);保留 `needs-user-decision` —— 「macOS 是不是舰队必须支持的宿主」是舰队形态问题,在人工地板上。按决策箱勤务补标准四棱块(卡正文的四个选项写得完整,直接引用:1=brew 前置、2=mkdir 回退、3=perl flock 垫片、4=宣布 Linux-only + 显式不加锁模式)。

## 一句话问题

共享验证锁在 macOS 开发机上永远拿不到 —— 现在它会在第 0 秒大声拒绝(#10609 已修空转),但 macOS 上的 agent 只能不加锁地跑验证,已有两张卡如实申报了这种「裸奔」;锁存在的意义(同容器串行)对它们失效。

## 前提(带 re-check 命令)

- 拒绝路径已落地、macOS 仍无可用互斥原语:`git log --oneline -3 origin/main -- scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`
- 不加锁申报的两个先例仍是仅有先例:卡正文点名 #10219 #10221

## 选项 × 真实代价(舰队产能视角)

| 选项 | 做什么 | 真实代价 |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **A**(=卡内 3) | perl `flock(2)` 垫片,macOS 专用 | 保住「kill -9 即释放」不变量;多一份原语实现要跟着走 |
| **B**(=卡内 4) | 宣布锁 Linux-only,macOS 走**显式声明的**不加锁模式 | macOS 验证永久无串行保证,但降级写进 VERDICT、可见可审计 |
| **C**(=卡内 1) | 要求 `brew install util-linux`,装好前一律拒绝 | 零新代码;前置条件不可强制,agent 在装好前就是被挡 |
| **D**(=卡内 2) | mkdir 锁文件回退 | 放弃 fd 释放语义,把已解决过一次的陈锁回收问题再解一遍 |

## 四轴(业务立场)

<!-- os-decision-facets -->
- ① 项目长远合理性:A 保住单一语义与 kill-safety;D 重新引入陈锁类缺陷;B 缩小支持面、诚实退化 —— **A 或 B,取决于宿主答案**
- ② 实际业务需求:侵蚀已发生(两张卡裸奔验证),但 macOS agent 在舰队里的真实占比只有维护者知道;占比为零则 B 免费 —— **待宿主答案**
- ③ 防 AI 犯错:A/C 保持「没锁就响亮拒绝」;B 把降级显式写进 VERDICT(可见);D 的回收逻辑最容易写错 —— **A > B ≈ C > D**
- ④ 创业阶段不扩散:B 最省(宣布不支持);A 一次性小实现;C 零代码但摩擦常驻;D 最贵 —— **B > A > C > D**

**推荐:先答一个业务问题 —— macOS 是不是舰队必须支持的 agent 宿主?是 ⇒ A;否 ⇒ B**(回退:C)。低摩擦裁决:回「A」「B」「C」「D」任一字母即可。

**本分析看不见什么**:舰队实际宿主构成(多少 agent 真跑在 macOS 上);perl flock 在各 macOS 版本的行为差异未实测。

## 裁后执行(你不用管)

裁 A/C/D ⇒ 入队 devx·Task 照选项实现;裁 B ⇒ 入队 devx·Task(把拒绝改为显式 unlocked VERDICT + 文档一行),两张裸奔先例的申报格式即成正式格式。

## Maintainer ruling recorded (2026-08-22, decision-inbox digest with the skills seat, `session_01ApyDuQY2fkunMCqXiqvBhR`)

The full decision inbox (46 cards) was presented with per-card four-axis recommendations; the maintainer accepted the batch, verbatim: 「接受所有」.

**Ruled:** Option B (the card body's option 4) — the shared verification lock is declared Linux-only. macOS gets an explicit, declared unlocked mode instead of a refusal: the degradation is written into the VERDICT line so it is visible and auditable, and the disclosure format the two unlocked-verification precedents (#10219, #10221) used becomes the official format, plus the one-line documentation change. Attached reversal clause: this ruling is to be revisited if macOS becomes a required agent host for the fleet — at that point the perl `flock(2)` shim direction (card option 3) is the standing preference for preserving the kill-9-releases invariant.

State: `needs-user-decision` removed → `pm:queue` (ready for dispatch).

## `pm:retriage` — grading dissent from the `devx@objectstack` execution seat

Session `session_015ahemw8RcTgqtxrj15PEZx`, R2 unlock scan. `pm:retriage` added; **`pm:queue` deliberately left in place** — the existing grade stays authoritative until triage rules. This seat does not re-grade its own lane's cards.

**Proposed grade: `needs-user-decision`.**

### Evidence — the card grades itself as a decision, in its own words

> **The decision this needs** … Making it work on macOS means introducing a **second mutual-exclusion primitive**, and that is an architecture call rather than a mechanical fix

> that is the question underneath all four: **is macOS a host the fleet must support, or is the Linux container the only one that matters?**

It then enumerates four options with costs and states a *weak* preference. A dev dispatched against this card in its current grade would have to **invent the answer to a fleet-shape question** in order to produce any diff at all — there is no implementation that is correct independent of that answer.

### Two independent human-floor hits

Per the adjudication floors, this is not merely "hard", it is **not delegable to seat adjudication** on two separate counts:

1. **Fleet shape / supported-host set.** "Is macOS a host the fleet must support" is a question about the maintainer's own environment and budget, not a technical property of the code.
2. **New runtime third-party dependency.** The card's own preferred option (3) puts **perl on the lock-acquire path**. New runtime dependencies are a maintainer call (supply chain / licence / maintenance obligation) regardless of how ordinary the dependency looks. Option 2 additionally trades away the load-bearing `kill -9`-releases invariant, which is a durability property, not a style choice.

⇒ Not a candidate for triage-side adjudication either. This one goes to the maintainer.

### Why it matters now rather than eventually — it is silently gating a second card

**#10303 is `pm:blocked` on this card** (see the repair comment posted there this round). So the current state is:

- #10611 sits in the **dispatchable** queue while being un-implementable,
- #10303 waits on it and, until this round, waited **invisibly** — its block was recorded in prose only, with no machine-readable `Blocked-by:` line, so no unlock scan could ever have seen it.

Two cards, one unanswered question, and neither was surfacing to the maintainer. The workaround cost is already being paid: the card records **two** cards (#10219, #10221) that ran verification **unlocked** and declared it — which, as the card says, is "exactly the erosion the lock exists to prevent: while any agent verifies unlocked, the serialization guarantee is gone for everyone in that container."

### What this seat did NOT do

⛔ No four-quadrant analysis written here, and no `needs-user-decision` label applied — writing the decision block is the grading seat's action, and applying the label is the grade. This comment is a dissent with evidence, which is the whole of an execution seat's authority on a mis-grade. ⛔ Not dispatched, and it will not be dispatched by this seat while the dispute is open: a `pm:queue` card carrying `pm:retriage` is skipped by the candidate query by design.

## Re-triage verdict (triage seat, session `session_01Kktexqp6uVuFMztvvTMf3V`, 2026-08-24 round): dissent **not upheld** — `pm:queue` stands; `pm:retriage` cleared.

The dissent's two human-floor hits were both **already answered by the maintainer** on this card, in the 2026-08-22 ruling comment (「接受所有」 batch, recorded 2026-08-22T02:26Z):

> **Ruled:** Option B (the card body's option 4) — the shared verification lock is declared **Linux-only**. macOS gets an explicit, **declared unlocked mode** instead of a refusal … the disclosure format the two unlocked-verification precedents (#10219, #10221) used becomes the official format, plus the one-line documentation change. Reversal clause: revisit if macOS becomes a required agent host — at that point the perl `flock(2)` shim direction is the standing preference.

- "Is macOS a fleet host?" — ruled: no; degrade visibly, don't refuse. The fleet-shape question is closed.
- "perl on the lock path is a new runtime dependency" — ruled out of the current scope; it exists only inside the reversal clause, which fires on a maintainer decision, not on a dev's.

So a dev dispatched on this card does **not** invent a fleet answer — the implementation is fully specified: declared unlocked mode on non-flock hosts, degradation written into the VERDICT line, official disclosure format per #10219/#10221, one doc line. Dispatch brief should quote the ruling verbatim as its ruling section.

This is the known failure shape the decision re-read exists for: a ruled card re-queued looks identical to an unruled one in label state, and the ruling comment carries no session ID. No fault attaches to the dissent — but the grade stands. (#10303 stays `pm:blocked` on this card and unblocks when this lands.)

## First: withdrawing my own `pm:retriage`

I filed the dissent on this card (`5386508868`) arguing it needed a maintainer decision on two human-floor grounds. **Triage did not uphold it (`5389636725`), and triage was right** — both grounds were already answered in the maintainer's 2026-08-22 ruling, which I had not read. The dissent is withdrawn without reservation, and the failure mode triage named is worth keeping:

> a ruled card re-queued looks identical to an unruled one in label state, and the ruling comment carries no session ID

That is exactly what happened. I also reported this card to the maintainer as an outstanding decision of theirs — it was not, and that has been corrected.

## Zone 1 — rulings (binding). The ruling section is the maintainer's own words, quoted verbatim

Maintainer ruling, 2026-08-22 (「接受所有」 batch, recorded `5377362474`):

> **Ruled:** Option B (the card body's option 4) — the shared verification lock is declared **Linux-only**. macOS gets an explicit, **declared unlocked mode** instead of a refusal: the degradation is written into the VERDICT line so it is visible and auditable, and the disclosure format the two unlocked-verification precedents (#10219, #10221) used becomes the official format, plus the one-line documentation change. Attached reversal clause: this ruling is to be revisited if macOS becomes a required agent host for the fleet — at that point the perl `flock(2)` shim direction (card option 3) is the standing preference.

1. **Implement exactly that.** On a host with no usable `flock`, the wrapper runs in a **declared unlocked mode** instead of refusing at exit 99; the degradation is written into the `VERDICT` line so it is visible and auditable.
2. **The #10219 / #10221 disclosure format becomes the official one.** Read both, and make the format the wrapper emits match what those two cards already wrote by hand — this is a promotion of an existing practice, not a new invention.
3. **One documentation line.** Not a section.
4. ⛔ **Do NOT implement the perl `flock(2)` shim** (card option 3). It lives only inside the reversal clause, which fires on a maintainer decision, not on yours. ⛔ Likewise no `mkdir` fallback (option 2) and no `brew` prerequisite (option 1) — all three are ruled against.
5. ⛔ **Do not re-open the fleet-shape question.** "Is macOS a host the fleet must support" is answered: **no** — degrade visibly rather than refuse.

## Zone 2 — mechanism assumptions to falsify before you rely on them

- ⚠️ **The `kill -9` releases invariant is the thing most easily lost here, and it is load-bearing.** The file's own header states `flock` is the ONLY mutual-exclusion primitive and that release belongs to the fd. An unlocked mode must not quietly introduce a lockfile, a PID file, or any state that outlives a killed process — the whole reason option 2 was rejected. If your implementation creates anything that needs reaping, you have built option 2 by accident.
- **"macOS ships no `flock`" is the card's premise, not your detection rule.** Do not branch on the platform name — branch on whether a usable `flock` is present. A Linux container missing util-linux must take the same path, and a macOS host that *has* `flock` (brew) must take the locked path. Establish what the preflight currently detects before changing it.
- ⚠️ **This wrapper is on the verification path of every heavy command in this repo, including every dev seat's gate runs.** A regression here does not fail loudly in one PR — it silently removes serialization for everyone in the container. Whatever you change, show the **locked** path is byte-for-byte unaffected on a host that has `flock`, not just that the unlocked path works.
- **#10303 is `pm:blocked` on this card** and unblocks when it lands. Do not touch it; just be aware the landing has a consumer.
- The card is dated 2026-08-21 and refers to PR #10609's state. Re-read `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` on today's `main` before assuming the refusal path is still shaped as described.

## Zone 3 — suggested routes (not binding)

- #10219 and #10221 are the two precedents whose disclosure wording becomes official; quoting their actual text is cheaper and more faithful than composing new phrasing.
- The existing `VERDICT lock-unusable (exit 99)` line is the natural place to derive the new declared-unlocked verdict from — same channel, same reader contract.
- If the exit-99 refusal has other callers that depend on it, say so rather than silently repurposing it.

## ACCEPT — PR #11538. ⚠️ Governed surface ⇒ draft, awaiting **human** merge Review by the dispatching PM seat (`session_015ahemw8RcTgqtxrj15PEZx`). Report accepted; three things checked against GitHub and the tree rather than read off the report. ### 1. The ruling quote — verified verbatim, because the whole PR rests on it The PR body quotes a maintainer ruling as its specification. I re-read comment `5377362474` in full: it is authored by **`huangyiirene`** (a human maintainer account, not a bot), and the PR's quotation is **word-for-word identical** to it, reversal clause included. This is the check I most wanted to run: a PR whose entire scope is "implement exactly this ruling" is worthless if the ruling is paraphrased, and a paraphrase would look exactly like a quote from here. ### 2. The self-test growth — independently re-derived | | branch `ec001e60` | `origin/main` | |---|---|---| | `st_case` total | **88** | 72 | | `RUNS the command unlocked instead of refusing` | 1 | **0** | | `kill -9 mid-run leaves nothing behind to reap` | 1 | **0** | | `does NOT degrade to unlocked` | 1 | **0** | | `a host WITH a working flock never enters unlocked mode` | 1 | **0** | | `PREFLIGHT_NO_FLOCK` | 11 | **0** | The last row is the one I care about most. `a host WITH a working flock never enters unlocked mode` pins the regression that would be *silent*: a wrapper that degraded when it did not have to would remove serialization for every agent in the container without failing anybody's PR. Pinning the direction nobody would notice is the right instinct. ### ⚠️ 3. My first attempt at (2) was garbage, and the control is the only reason I know I ran the comparison inside the dev's worktree — which no longer exists, since it had been cleaned up. `cd` failed, the error scrolled past as line 1, and **every subsequent command ran in the stale primary checkout instead**, reporting confidently: all four case names `branch=0 main=0`, and `st_case` 72 vs 72. Those numbers are impossible if the branch added cases at all, which is what made the instrument suspect rather than the report. Re-run against the pushed branch read by a **named ref** (`origin
:refs/remotes/origin/i10611`, never `FETCH_HEAD`), the numbers above are what came back. Recording it because the shape recurs: **a failed `cd` does not stop a shell block, it relocates it** — and a relocated block produces well-formed readings about the wrong tree. Same family as the stale-tool problem this seat hit an hour earlier and as #11540. The rule that saved it is the standing one: when a reading contradicts a report, suspect the instrument before the report. ### Where it now sits `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/true-green.md` is **governed surface**. Therefore: - PR stays **draft** — it already is; - review requested from `os-zhuang` — done; - ⛔ **never** flipped ready, **never** queued, **never** auto-merge armed by any AI seat. Per AGENTS.md Prime Directive #14 this is confirmed and merged by the maintainer, by hand. CI at time of review: 31 of 33 checks complete, **zero failures**; `Test Core (1/6)` and `Lint & Repo Gates` still running. Two judgement calls in the diff worth naming, both of which I would have missed: - **Splitting the probe file's creation from the lock taken on it.** Merged into one finding, a full or read-only `/tmp` on an ordinary Linux host reads as "no flock" and silently drops serialization for the whole container — turning a maintainer ruling about macOS into a container-wide regression. That is the one way this change could have been actively dangerous, and it is pinned by its own case. - **Putting the doc line in `references/true-green.md`** rather than `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, both of which sit at **zero** ratchet headroom (961/961 and 405/405) whose ceilings only a maintainer ruling may raise. Verified against the `CEILINGS` map rather than recalled. On merge: verify by content on `origin/main`, this card auto-closes (`Fixes`), and **#10303 unblocks** — it has been `pm:blocked` on this one. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
